title: In the deformation's "All at once" mode, the cards show pictures that never appear, and the last card is not the main picture
detail: With All at once, the main plane shows H_t = h_{n,t} ∘ … ∘ h_{1,t}. Every card is labelled "t = 0.50", but card k draws h_{k,t} ∘ F_{k−1}: its own step at t on top of the earlier steps already finished (cardDef uses homF(k, t) ∘ stageF(k − 1), and cardT gives every step the same t). So at t = 0.5 the f₃ card is a compact shape, while the main plane shows a shape spanning Re w from −3 to 1. This breaks the design's own rule in 2.2: "the last step's card equals the main picture". A student reading the row as "the chain at t = 0.5" sees intermediate states that the deformation never passes through. One after another (sequential) mode is consistent: the current step's card equals the main picture.
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/shots/m3-def-allatonce.png (exp · Möbius · zeros and poles, All at once, T = 0.5). __cmwCards(): every card has t 0.5; card 3's view is centred at −1.30 + 1.05i with s 20.5, and the main plane is centred at 0.2 + 0.1i. Code: src/app.js:6269 cardT, src/app.js:6351 cardDef.
fix: When allAtOnce(), card k should draw the all-at-once map up to k: h_{k,t} ∘ … ∘ h_{1,t} (map mode 3 with a = 0, b = k, t). Its grey start should be h_{k−1,t} ∘ … ∘ h_{1,t}. Then the last card equals the main plane at every t. Add a test that compares the last card's map with morphState(false).F at three values of t.

title: A bound field silently keeps an old value when its number leaves the field's range (r = a with a < 0), so the picture depends on how the slider moved
detail: When a disc's radius is bound to a and a becomes −0.3, applyBinds skips the out-of-range value and keeps the radius the last valid value gave. The Shapes list then shows Disc 1 |z| < 0.2 while Parameters shows a = −0.3. Nothing marks the disc as invalid. The radius left behind depends on the slide: a slow drag through 0.01 leaves r = 0.01, and a jump from 0.5 leaves r = 0.5. So the same state (a = −0.3) has different pictures, which contradicts the constructions design's rule "No result depends on history". The stale radius is also saved, so links and reloads carry it. Integer fields are affected in the same way (n, nc and nr are clamped to 1–60 and rounded without a note).
evidence: Measured in the app (test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m2_params.js): a = 0.5 → r 0.5; a = 0.2 → r 0.2; a = −0.3 → r stays 0.2, with bind {r: 'a'} and the curve Re z = a correctly at −0.3. Screenshot: test/mathrev_cdp/shots/m2-disc-neg.png (Shapes row "|z| < 0.2", slider a = −0.3). Code: src/app.js:12920 BIND_LIM, src/app.js:12921 applyBinds ("keeps the field's last value").
fix: Make an out-of-range value a defined state, not a skip. Mark the shape undefined and do not draw it. Its row should give the reason ("r = a = −0.3: a radius must be positive"), as the constructions design does for an undefined point. The shape comes back as soon as a is valid again. Never keep a value that the formula no longer gives.

title: Opening a state does not recompute numbers by formula or bound fields, so a figure can open inconsistent with its own formulas
detail: Only onParamChange calls applyBinds, and Params.recompute() runs only on an edit. A saved state, link or scene whose stored values disagree with the formulas opens as stored. The example is b = 2a + 1 with a = 0.5 saved as b = 7: b stays 7, and a disc bound to b keeps r = 0.5. This happens with a hand-edited scene file, a file from another build, or the stale values of math-2. The values in a link are otherwise exact: the round trip of steps, shapes and numbers matched to the bit (see math-11).
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m2_params.js, case d5: params after load [{a 0.5}, {b: expr '2a + 1', value 7}], disc r 0.5. grep: applyBinds is called only at src/app.js:12963-12964 (onParamChange).
fix: After sanitizeState, and in openFigure, undo and redo, run Params.recompute() and then applyBinds(x, null) on every shape and target, before the first render. The formulas are the source of truth, and the stored values are only a cache.

title: The reference guide says the clicked point becomes a zero of F; with a step after f_k it does not
detail: "Add zero of f_k here" puts ζ = F_{k−1}(z), so z becomes a zero of F_k, exactly. If later steps follow, F(z) = f_n ∘ … ∘ f_{k+1}(0), which is generally not 0. Example: zeros and poles, then exp. After Add zero of f₁ here at z = 0.8 + 0.6i, F₁(z) = 0 but F(z) = e⁰ = 1. The guide states unconditionally that "the point becomes a zero of F exactly". The menu gives no hint either, although its head shows F(z) and the user will check it. The design (2.5) says it correctly: "a zero of F_k, and of F when the step is last". The tour's wording is correct only because its scene ends with f₁.
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m1_menu.js, scenario B_zp_exp: zeros "2, 0.8+0.6i", F₁(z) = [0, 0], F(z) = [1, 0]. Guide text: src/app.js:11660. Tour: src/tour.js:168-169.
fix: Guide: "…so the point becomes a zero of f_k ∘ … ∘ f₁, and of F when f_k is the last step". Menu: when active steps follow k, add a muted line under the item, such as "F there: 1 (f₂ follows)". Compute it with rangeF(k, n)(0).

title: "Add pole of f_k here" omits the "also at" line, although the same other points become poles
detail: A pole put at w = F_{k−1}(z) is a pole of F_k at every preimage of w, just as a zero is. After exp, Add pole of f₃ here makes poles at z + 2πik for every integer k. The menu says so only for the zero item. A student adding one pole after exp gets a column of poles with no explanation.
evidence: src/planemenu.js:277 (": kind === 'zeros' ? also : null"). test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m1_menu.js scenario A: "Add zero of f₃ here / also at z + 2πik", and "Add pole of f₃ here" with no line.
fix: Show alsoAt(j, k) for both kinds (the full-list message still takes precedence).

title: A degenerate Möbius step (ad − bc = 0, reached by sliding a shared number) still draws a pole at −d/c
detail: With c₁ = a and a = 1, f₁ = (z + 1)/(z + 1) ≡ 1. The Inspector notes "a₁d₁ − b₁c₁ = 0", and the F tile correctly lights Rational, deg 0. But X still shows the red pole cross at z = −1, in X → Y and in Phase, and so does the Region card. The singularity is removable, so a constant map has no pole. Sliding a through 1 is now a one-gesture way to meet this. The zeros-and-poles step handles the same situation correctly ("A zero and a pole cancel at 1.").
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/shots/m2-mob-degenerate.png and m2-mob-degenerate-phase.png (a = 1; the × at −1 on X and on the Region card). F(0.3 + 0.2i) = F(−0.7 + 0.9i) = 1 (measured).
fix: When CX.mobDetZero(m) holds, omit the pole mark and its cut and fold markers. Under the Inspector note, add "f₁ is constant (= a/c); z = −d/c is removable". Use the same rule for the menu's "also at" line: F_{k−1} is constant there, so an added zero makes F ≡ 0. Today the line says only "other points may map here too".

title: Zeros added from the menu keep binary rounding noise in their text, and it shows in the Inspector's fields
detail: The mark is stored at full double precision, which keeps F_k(z) = 0 exact. The cost is fields that read "0.5800000000000001+0.96i" (from z² + 0.3 at the snapped z = 0.8 + 0.6i, where the exact value is 0.58 + 0.96i), "0.8500000000000002+1.32i" and "0.8+5.551115123125783e-17i" (Joukowski on |z| = 1, where the value is exactly real). The TeX head rounds them to 0.58, so the field and the formula disagree.
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m1_menu.js scenarios D, E, F (zpParams). test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m5_field.js: the Inspector field values ["3", "0.5800000000000001+0.96i"], with the head formula showing 0.58.
fix: Before Funcs.zpItem, round each part to 15 significant digits (+x.toPrecision(15)), and set a part to 0 when it is below 1e-15·|w|. The error this adds to F_k(z) is under 1e-15, invisible at any zoom the app allows, and the field then reads 0.58+0.96i.

title: The menu head prints rounding noise as a value: "F(z) = −2.20 + 5.55×10⁻¹⁷i" and "F(z) = −2.0000000000"
detail: For Joukowski at z = 0.8 + 0.6i (|z| = 1), J(z) = 0.8 is real. The head prints the floating-point residue of the imaginary part in scientific notation, because fmtR switches to ×10ⁿ for any nonzero value below the display precision. For a constant F, the decimals come from Y's scale (dpFor(api.scale('R'))), and Y has auto-fitted to a point (math-9), so the head prints 10 decimals.
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m1_menu.js: F_jouk_zp head "F(z) = −2.20 + 5.55×10−17i"; C_mobdeg_zp head "F(z) = −2.0000000000". Code: src/planemenu.js:32-48 (dpFor, fmtR, fmtCx).
fix: Treat a component as 0 when it is below 1e-12 of the larger one. Cap the decimals at 6, or derive them from X's pixel size times |F′(z)| rather than from Y's scale.

title: When a shared number makes F constant, Y auto-fits to a window of 2×10⁻¹⁶ per division
detail: A constant image (degenerate Möbius, or a zero and a pole cancelling) is a single point. Y's fit then zooms to the rounding scale and labels the axes 6×10⁻¹⁶ … −6×10⁻¹⁶. With a slider this is easy to pass through, and the view jumps by 15 orders of magnitude and back. This probably predates v15 for a typed constant, but v15 makes it a one-gesture event.
fix: Give the fit a floor relative to the point, for example a half-width of at least 1e-6·max(1, |w|). Or keep the previous Y window while the image is degenerate.

title: Links and scene files do not carry the Landscape camera or the deformation's time, so the recipient sees a different picture
detail: The figure itself round-trips exactly. Steps, shapes, shared numbers (including 1/3 and a number by formula) and F at a test point were identical after Copy link → open. But the Landscape camera came back at the defaults (yaw −38°, pitch 30°, against the sent 0.7 and 0.9 rad). The deformation also came back closed at T = 0, against open at T = 1.25. A teacher who sends "look at this relief from here" or "pause at t = 0.25" loses that.
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m4_link.js: same = true and F_before = F_after = −0.10437028474356924 + 0.19509803028053666i. camBefore yaw 0.7 and pitch 0.9 against camAfter −0.6632 and 0.5236; morphAfter {open: false, T: 0}. figureState (src/app.js:12986) has no camera (figHasCam false in m3).
fix: Add the cameras (yaw, pitch, dist relative to the fit, tx, ty) and the deformation (open, T, homAll) to figureState, and restore them in openFigure. Saved state can keep its current behaviour if that is intended.

title: The Inspector's formula replaces shared numbers with their values, so the dependence disappears
detail: With ζ₁ = a, the f₃ head reads w₃ = (w₂ − 0.5)/(w₂ + 0.5i). With c₁ = a, the Möbius head reads (z + 1)/(z + 1). The design's point is that a plain a is the shared number, and the formula is where a student sees what a controls. Expr.toTex already prints a name node as its name.
fix: When a field holds names, build the step's TeX from the field's AST (names kept), for example w₃ = (w₂ − a)/(w₂ + 0.5i) and (z + 1)/(az + 1). The values can stay in a tooltip or in the F tile's table.

title: The "also at" line falls back to a vague note for common maps where the other points are known
detail: After sin, the line reads "other points may map here too", but the other points are π − z + 2πk and z + 2πk. The same holds for cos (−z + 2πk), the principal z^α with real α (e^{2πik/α}z on its sheet) and the constant case of math-6. For a polynomial step, "also at n other points" counts with multiplicity, so at a critical point there are fewer distinct points. The cases the design names are all correct, checked numerically at z = 0.8 + 0.6i: F₃(z + 2πi) = 5·10⁻¹⁷ after exp; F(−z) = 0 after z²; F(1/z) = 2·10⁻¹⁶ after Joukowski; F(e^{2πi/3}z) = 1.6·10⁻¹⁵ after z³; and F(π − z) = 2·10⁻¹⁶ after sin, which the menu does not mention.
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/cmd/m1_menu.js scenarios A, D, F, I, J, K (Fk_at). src/planemenu.js:51-80 (symOf, alsoAt).
fix: Add symOf entries for sin ("π − z + 2πk, z + 2πk") and cos ("−z + 2πk"). Say "every point" when an earlier step is constant. Say "other points (with multiplicity)" for polynomial and rational steps, or count distinct preimages numerically.

title: A constant F shows dark speckles along the Phase outline at rest
detail: With F ≡ 1 (degenerate Möbius through a = 1), the Phase view and the f₁ card draw dark dashes along the rectangle's right, top and bottom edges. These are likely rounding noise on the |F| = 1 band boundary, or the outline's casing evaluated on a degenerate map. A rest frame should show a clean outline on a uniform colour.
evidence: test/mathrev_cdp/shots/m2-mob-degenerate-phase.png and m2-mob-degenerate-phase-zoom.png (crop of the main plane, 3× nearest).
fix: Skip modulus band edges where |F| is constant to within 1e-12, or snap |F| to 1 when within a few ulps. Check whether the outline's casing takes this path.

title: Parameters print negative numbers with a hyphen-minus ("-0.3", "-2")
detail: The value field and the slider's range labels show "-0.3" and "-2". Everywhere else the app writes the real minus sign (U+2212), as in the menu head and the rulers. The range labels are not inputs, so they can use U+2212 freely. The field can display it too (the parser accepts it).
fix: Format the range labels and the idle field with I18N.num(...).replace('-', '−'), as planemenu.js fmtR does.
